summary.text: Temperate climates are found in the middle latitudes, roughly 23.5° to 66.5° north or south of the Equator, between the tropics and the polar regions.
Compared with tropical climates, they usually have wider temperature ranges through the year and more distinct seasons.
Besides latitude, sea currents, prevailing winds, the size of the landmass and altitude all shape what a temperate place is like.

facts.label: North temperate zone
facts.value: Tropic of Cancer to the Arctic Circle

items.prompt: Hills in coastal California turn brown every summer and green again in winter. What rainfall pattern explains this?

options.label: Dry all year with rare storms

items.explain: Coastal California has a Mediterranean climate, which has a dry summer and a wet winter.

items.prompt: Two temperate cities share a latitude: one on a coast fed by cool ocean air, one deep inside a huge continent. Which gets the hotter summers and colder winters?

options.label: The coastal city, from damp sea air
The inland city, far from the sea
Whichever one sits at lower altitude

items.explain: Onshore flow from cool oceans gives mild summers and cool winters, while large land masses create a hot summer and a cold winter.

items.prompt: In some monsoon areas of southern China, how much of the year's precipitation falls in the five warmest months?
items.explain: These subtropical monsoon areas have a sharp wet-dry pattern, with very heavy summer rain and chilly, dry winters.

items.prompt: What brings the dry summers to places with a Mediterranean climate?

options.label: Dry winds from deserts on the side nearer the equator
Cold polar air that is too chilly to hold moisture
High mountains that block every wind off the sea
Sea water that grows too warm to make any clouds

items.explain: Mediterranean regions border arid deserts on their equatorward side, and those deserts bring the dry winds behind the summer dry season.

items.prompt: An oceanic-climate town sits much closer to the pole than most others of its type. What should it expect compared with them?
items.explain: Subpolar oceanic areas sit on the cool end of oceanic climates, and snowfall is more common there than in other oceanic climates.

items.prompt: A city lies at 30° N, in the warm band of the temperate zone nearest the tropics. What kind of weather is unusual there?
items.explain: Between 23.5° and 35° the temperate zone is strongly influenced by the tropics, and freezing precipitation is uncommon there.
